claim: The amyloid β peptide (Aβ) is a key player in the etiology of Alzheimer disease (AD).
source: The amyloid β peptide (Aβ) is a key player in the etiology of Alzheimer disease (AD), yet a systematic investigation of its molecular interactions has not been reported.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus in the field of Alzheimer's disease research.

claim: A systematic investigation of Aβ molecular interactions has not been reported.
source: The amyloid β peptide (Aβ) is a key player in the etiology of Alzheimer disease (AD), yet a systematic investigation of its molecular interactions has not been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature at the time of publication.

claim: Somatostatin-14 (SST14) was the most selectively enriched oAβ1-42 binder identified by quantitative mass spectrometry.
source: Remarkably, the cyclic neuroendocrine peptide somatostatin-14 (SST14) was observed to be the most selectively enriched oAβ1-42 binder.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry analysis of proteins binding to oligomeric Aβ1-42.

claim: The binding interface between SST14 and Aβ1-42 comprises a central tryptophan within SST14 and the N-terminus of Aβ1-42.
source: The binding interface comprises a central tryptophan within SST14 and the N-terminus of Aβ1-42.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mutagenesis studies and binding assays showing the requirement of tryptophan-8 in SST14 and the N-terminus of Aβ1-42.

claim: The presence of SST14 inhibited Aβ aggregation.
source: The presence of SST14 inhibited Aβ aggregation and masked the ability of several antibodies to detect Aβ.
evidence: This is supported by Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data showing extended lag phases in Aβ aggregation when SST14 is present.

claim: The presence of SST14 masked the ability of several antibodies to detect Aβ.
source: The presence of SST14 inhibited Aβ aggregation and masked the ability of several antibodies to detect Aβ.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data showing reduced antibody detection of Aβ in the presence of SST14.

claim: Aβ1-42, but not Aβ1-40, formed oligomeric assemblies of 50 to 60 kDa in the presence of SST14.
source: Notably, Aβ1-42, but not Aβ1-40, formed in the presence of SST14 oligomeric assemblies of 50 to 60 kDa that were visualized by gel electrophoresis, nanoparticle tracking analysis and electron microscopy.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental techniques including gel electrophoresis, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and electron microscopy.

claim: The Aβ peptide represents a 37 to 49 amino acids endoproteolytic fragment of the amyloid precursor protein (APP).
source: The amyloid beta (Aβ) peptide represents a 37 to 49 amino acids endoproteolytic fragment of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), a single-span transmembrane protein, which in humans is coded on the long arm of Chromosome 21 within cytogenetic band q21.3 (Kang et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kang et al., 1987.

claim: APP is coded on the long arm of Chromosome 21 within cytogenetic band q21.3 in humans.
source: The amyloid beta (Aβ) peptide represents a 37 to 49 amino acids endoproteolytic fragment of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), a single-span transmembrane protein, which in humans is coded on the long arm of Chromosome 21 within cytogenetic band q21.3 (Kang et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kang et al., 1987.

claim: Fibrillary aggregates of Aβ represent the main constituents of extracellular amyloid plaques that accumulate in the brains of individuals afflicted with Alzheimer disease.
source: The cellular biology that governs the formation and clearance of Aβ has been understood to play a critical role in Alzheimer disease (AD) since it was shown that fibrillary aggregates of Aβ represent the main constituents of extracellular amyloid plaques that accumulate in the brains of individuals afflicted with the disease (Glenner and Wong, 1984).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Glenner and Wong, 1984.

claim: β- and γ-secretases are responsible for the cleavage reactions that cause the N- and C-terminal release of the Aβ peptide from its APP precursor.
source: The endoproteinases responsible for the release of Aβ are broadly referred to as secretases, with β- and γ-secretases being responsible for the critical cleavage reactions that cause the N- and C-terminal release of the Aβ peptide from its APP precursor, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of Alzheimer's disease research.

claim: Mutations in the human APP gene cause an increase in Aβ levels or shift the balance of Aβ peptides of different lengths in favor of the production of Aβ1-42.
source: Mutations in the human APP gene (Goate et al., 1991) or the genes coding for presenilin 1 or 2, catalytic subunits of γ-secretases (Rogaev et al., 1995; Sherrington et al., 1995), which cause an increase in Aβ levels or shift the balance of Aβ peptides of different lengths in favor of the production of Aβ1-42, remain the only known causes for early-onset familial manifestations of AD.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goate et al., 1991; Rogaev et al., 1995; Sherrington et al., 1995.

claim: Mutations in the genes coding for presenilin 1 or 2 cause an increase in Aβ levels or shift the balance of Aβ peptides of different lengths in favor of the production of Aβ1-42.
source: Mutations in the human APP gene (Goate et al., 1991) or the genes coding for presenilin 1 or 2, catalytic subunits of γ-secretases (Rogaev et al., 1995; Sherrington et al., 1995), which cause an increase in Aβ levels or shift the balance of Aβ peptides of different lengths in favor of the production of Aβ1-42, remain the only known causes for early-onset familial manifestations of AD.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rogaev et al., 1995; Sherrington et al., 1995.

claim: Mutations in APP or presenilin genes remain the only known causes for early-onset familial manifestations of AD.
source: Mutations in the human APP gene (Goate et al., 1991) or the genes coding for presenilin 1 or 2, catalytic subunits of γ-secretases (Rogaev et al., 1995; Sherrington et al., 1995), which cause an increase in Aβ levels or shift the balance of Aβ peptides of different lengths in favor of the production of Aβ1-42, remain the only known causes for early-onset familial manifestations of AD.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goate et al., 1991; Rogaev et al., 1995; Sherrington et al., 1995.

claim: Extracellular amyloid deposits are increasingly being viewed as innocuous sinks for misfolded Aβ.
source: Although the extracellular amyloid deposits themselves are increasingly being viewed as innocuous sinks for misfolded Aβ, they may continue to play a role as reservoirs from which monomeric or oligomeric Aβ, hereafter referred to as mAβ or oAβ (see also (Yang et al., 2017)), can emanate (Selkoe, 2001).
evidence: This reflects a shift in scientific understanding, supported by citation to Selkoe, 2001.

claim: Amyloid deposits may play a role as reservoirs from which monomeric or oligomeric Aβ can emanate.

evidence: This is supported by citation to Selkoe, 2001.

claim: Soluble forms of Aβ may interact with other molecules in the extracellular space.
source: These soluble forms of Aβ may interact with other molecules they meet in the extracellular space (Narayan et al., 2011), or may bind to molecules embedded in the plasma membrane (Laurén et al., 2009), which may be a precursor to their endocytosis (Jin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Narayan et al., 2011.

claim: Soluble forms of Aβ may bind to molecules embedded in the plasma membrane.
source: These soluble forms of Aβ may interact with other molecules they meet in the extracellular space (Narayan et al., 2011), or may bind to molecules embedded in the plasma membrane (Laurén et al., 2009), which may be a precursor to their endocytosis (Jin et al., 2016).

claim: Binding of Aβ to plasma membrane molecules may be a precursor to endocytosis.
source: These soluble forms of Aβ may interact with other molecules they meet in the extracellular space (Narayan et al., 2011), or may bind to molecules embedded in the plasma membrane (Laurén et al., 2009), which may be a precursor to their endocytosis (Jin et al., 2016).

claim: Aβ can reach the cytoplasm and associates with intracellular compartments, including mitochondria.
source: Although it is not known how precisely Aβ, which has been taken up into the cell by endocytosis, can overcome the bilayer that surrounds the endolysosomal vesiculo-tubular network, it is well established that the peptide can also reach the cytoplasm and associates with other intracellular compartments, including mitochondria (Lustbader et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lustbader et al., 2004.

claim: Aβ has been shown to interact with apolipoprotein E in the extracellular space.
source: Within the extracellular space, Aβ has, for instance, been shown to interact with apolipoproteins E (Strittmatter et al., 1993) and J (the latter is also known as clusterin) (Narayan et al., 2011; Ghiso et al., 1993).

claim: Certain polymorphisms in the genes coding for apolipoproteins E and J bestow an increased risk to develop late-onset AD.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Lambert et al., 2009; Harold et al., 2009; Corder et al., 1993.

claim: Exposure of neurons to soluble oAβ leads to the intracellular deposition of hyperphosphorylated tau in the form of neurofibrillary tangles (NFT).
source: When neurons are exposed to soluble oAβ, a cascade of events is thought to unfold, which leads to the intracellular deposition of hyperphosphorylated tau in the form of so-called neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) (Grundke-Iqbal et al., 1986a, 1986b).

evidence: This is supported by citations to Kohli et al., 2012; Bai et al., 2008.

claim: The top-listed 200 proteins co-enriched with biotin-oAβ1-42 showed highly significant overrepresentation of 'Cellular component' GO classifiers associated with 'extracellular vesicular exosome', 'cytosol', 'vesicle' and 'extracellular region part'.
source: This analysis revealed amongst the biotin-oAβ1-42 binding candidates a highly significant overrepresentation (p<1.0 E-50) of 'Cellular component' GO classifiers that indicate an association with the 'extracellular vesicular exosome', 'cytosol', 'vesicle' and 'extracellular region part' (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis of the experimental data, with results shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All top-listed 50 candidate interactors were identified on the basis of more than ten peptide-to-spectrum matches (PSMs).
source: A more detailed analysis of the list of biotin-oAβ1-42 (B-oAβ1-42) candidate interactors revealed that all top-listed 50 candidates were identified on the basis of more than ten peptide-to-spectrum matches (PSMs) and with sequence coverages exceeding 50% of their primary structures (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in Table 1.

claim: All top-listed 50 candidate interactors had sequence coverages exceeding 50% of their primary structures.

claim: The abundance levels of the top 50 candidate interactors in the B-oAβ1-42-specific samples exceeded their levels in the negative control sample by more than four-fold.
source: Moreover, indicative of high selectivity of the affinity capture procedures applied, the abundance levels of these 50 candidate interactors in the B-oAβ1-42-specific samples exceeded their levels in the negative control sample by more than four-fold.
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative mass spectrometry data from the interactome experiments.

claim: The Aβ peptide itself was amongst the proteins identified whose enrichment levels in specific versus unspecific affinity capture samples were most pronounced.

claim: Peroxiredoxin-5 exhibited the highest levels of B-oAβ1-42 co-enrichment.
source: The highest levels of B-oAβ1-42 co-enrichment were exhibited by peroxiredoxin-5, rab-1A, lactate dehydrogenase, hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase, ATP synthase subunits beta and gamma, and acyl CoA thioester hydrolase.

claim: ATP synthase was previously known to interact with Aβ peptides.

claim: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase was previously known to interact with Aβ peptides.

claim: A free N-terminus of Aβ1-42 might be critical for inducing neurofibrillary degeneration.
source: Observations by others, which preceded this study, have provoked a hypothesis that a free N-terminus of Aβ1-42 might be critical for inducing neurofibrillary degeneration (Jin et al., 2011) and synapse loss (Shankar et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jin et al., 2011; Shankar et al., 2008.

claim: A free N-terminus of Aβ1-42 might be critical for inducing synapse loss.

claim: When the C-terminally biotinylated oAβ1-42-B bait was employed for affinity capture, a lower number of proteins was consistently observed to co-enrich with the bait compared to N-terminally tagged B-oAβ1-42 bait.
source: When the C-terminally biotinylated oAβ1-42-B bait was employed for affinity capture, a lower number of proteins was consistently observed to co-enrich with the bait and their ratios of co-enrichment (relative to biotin-only negative controls) were generally lower than those observed with the N-terminally tagged B-oAβ1-42 bait (see also Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative interactome data from Experiments I and II.

claim: The ratios of co-enrichment of proteins with C-terminally biotinylated oAβ1-42-B bait were generally lower than those observed with the N-terminally tagged B-oAβ1-42 bait.
source: When the C-terminally biotinylated oAβ1-42-B bait was employed for affinity capture, a lower number of proteins was consistently observed to co-enrich with the bait and their ratios of co-enrichment (relative to biotin-only negative controls) were generally lower than those observed with the N-terminally tagged B-oAβ1-42 bait (see also Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative interactome data from Experiments I and II.

claim: The 'NFFWK' peptide could only have originated from preprosomatostatin or preprocortistatin.
source: A query of human genome databases revealed that this peptide, owing to its unusual composition, and despite its short length, could only have originated from the well-known paralogs preprosomatostatin or preprocortistatin (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on database searches and sequence analysis, with results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The 'NFFWK' peptide is naturally preceded by a tryptic cleavage site.
source: This conclusion was strengthened by the fact that this peptide is naturally preceded by a tryptic cleavage site and the exquisite match between observed and in silico predicted fragment ions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is an exquisite match between observed and in silico predicted fragment ions for the 'NFFWK' peptide.
source: This conclusion was strengthened by the fact that this peptide is naturally preceded by a tryptic cleavage site and the exquisite match between observed and in silico predicted fragment ions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Preprosomatostatin and preprocortistatin give rise to cyclic neuropeptide hormones through a series of posttranslational trimming steps.
source: Searching for a plausible explanation, it became apparent that preprosomatostatin and preprocortistatin give rise to cyclic neuropeptide hormones through a series of posttranslational trimming steps, and the 'NFFWK' peptide is the only tryptic peptide derived from the mature hormone that is of sufficient length and distinct sequence to be readily identifiable by MS (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the biosynthesis of somatostatin and cortistatin.

claim: The 'NFFWK' peptide is the only tryptic peptide derived from the mature SST/CST hormone that is of sufficient length and distinct sequence to be readily identifiable by MS.
source: Searching for a plausible explanation, it became apparent that preprosomatostatin and preprocortistatin give rise to cyclic neuropeptide hormones through a series of posttranslational trimming steps, and the 'NFFWK' peptide is the only tryptic peptide derived from the mature hormone that is of sufficient length and distinct sequence to be readily identifiable by MS (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The free N-terminus of Aβ1-42 is essential for the interaction with the 'NFFWK' peptide.
source: The subsequent application of an identical interactome analysis workflow as outlined above (but replacing TMT with iTRAQ isobaric labeling) (Figure 1A) corroborated the propensity of 'NFFWK' to bind to oAβ1-42-B but also established that the free N-terminus is indeed essential for this peptide-peptide interaction (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by the interactome data shown in Figure 2D comparing different Aβ bait constructs.

claim: Mature somatostatin represented the protein whose levels were most selectively enriched in oAβ1-42-B affinity capture eluates in Experiment III.
source: Although neither preprosomatostatin nor preprocortistatin had passed stringent filtering criteria required for inclusion in the Aβ interactome data tables (because their identification could not be based on at least three unique peptides with a minimum length of six amino acids), close inspection of Experiment III data under omission of these filters suggested that mature somatostatin was not only present in the dataset but represented the protein, whose levels were most selectively enriched in oAβ1-42-B affinity capture eluates.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the mass spectrometry data from Experiment III.

claim: The distributions of TMT signature ions derived from tryptic 'NFFWK' and 'TFTSC' peptides derived from the mature SST14 neuropeptide exhibited identical TMT signature ion profiles.
source: More specifically, consistent with the notion that Aβ1-42 interacts separately with the SST14 neuropeptide and preprosomatostatin precursor, the distributions of TMT signature ions derived from tryptic 'NFFWK' and 'TFTSC' peptides derived from the mature SST14 neuropeptide exhibited identical TMT signature ion profiles patterns that differed fundamentally from the respective TMT profiles of preprosomatostatin peptides which mapped to sequences upstream of the SST14 sequence domain (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by the TMT signature ion data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The TMT signature ion profiles of SST14-derived peptides differed fundamentally from the TMT profiles of preprosomatostatin peptides which mapped to sequences upstream of the SST14 sequence domain.
source: More specifically, consistent with the notion that Aβ1-42 interacts separately with the SST14 neuropeptide and preprosomatostatin precursor, the distributions of TMT signature ions derived from tryptic 'NFFWK' and 'TFTSC' peptides derived from the mature SST14 neuropeptide exhibited identical TMT signature ion profiles patterns that differed fundamentally from the respective TMT profiles of preprosomatostatin peptides which mapped to sequences upstream of the SST14 sequence domain (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by the TMT signature ion data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No peptides were observed that could be uniquely assigned to preprocortistatin.
source: In agreement with the interpretation that the 'NFFWK' had probably originated from SST14, not CST17, no peptides were observed in this or other experiments that could be uniquely assigned to preprocortistatin.
evidence: This is based on the absence of specific peptides in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: The 'NFFWK' peptide binds preferentially to oligomeric (pre-aggregated) but not monomeric Aβ1-42-biotin.
source: Finally, these experiments repeatedly established that the 'NFFWK' peptide binds preferentially to oligomeric (pre-aggregated) but not monomeric Aβ1-42-biotin (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative binding data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: oAβ1-42 preparations gave rise to a pronounced signal of high molecular mass (HMM) when analyzed by denaturing SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with the 6E10 antibody.
source: For this experiment, oAβ1-42 preparations (generated by incubating mAβ1-42 purified by gel filtration at 37°C for 2 hr with shaking at the speed of 700 rpm) gave rise to a pronounced signal of high molecular mass (HMM), not seen with mAβ1-42, when analyzed by denaturing SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with the 6E10 antibody directed against an N-terminal Aβ1-42 epitope (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Biotin-SST14 affinity capture matrices exposed to oAβ1-42 showed robust 6E10 signals both in the HMM and low mass region of the blot.
source: The analysis revealed in samples which had been exposed to oAβ1-42 robust 6E10 signals both in the HMM and low mass region of the blot, the latter migrating at the same level as mAβ1-42.
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the biotin-SST14 affinity capture experiment.

claim: Very little low mass signal was observed in biotin-SST14 affinity capture samples which had been incubated with mAβ1-42.
source: Because very little low mass signal was observed in samples, which had been incubated with mAβ1-42, we concluded that the low mass signal in oAβ1-42 exposed samples most likely reflected a release of a fraction of Aβ1-42 molecules from SST14-bound oAβ1-42 aggregates under the harsh denaturing analysis conditions.
evidence: This is based on Western blot data from the biotin-SST14 affinity capture experiment.

claim: SST14 binding only occurs when Aβ1-42 is available in oligomeric form.
source: Taken together, this experiment validated that SST14 binding only occurs when Aβ1-42 is available in oligomeric form and established a direct mode of interaction.
evidence: This is based on the biotin-SST14 affinity capture experiments showing binding to oAβ1-42 but not mAβ1-42.

claim: The interaction between SST14 and Aβ1-42 is direct.
source: Taken together, this experiment validated that SST14 binding only occurs when Aβ1-42 is available in oligomeric form and established a direct mode of interaction.
evidence: This is based on the biotin-SST14 affinity capture experiments using synthetic peptides without co-factors.

claim: Mixing Edans-SST14 donor and Aβ1-42-TMR acceptor peptides caused profound quenching of the donor signal, concomitant with an increase in acceptor fluorescence.
source: Mixing of the two peptides caused profound quenching of the donor signal, concomitant with an increase in acceptor fluorescence, indicating energy transfer.
evidence: This is supported by the FRET data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A half-maximal effective concentration of 12.7 μM SST14 was deduced for restoring donor fluorescence in the FRET competition experiment.
source: A half-maximal effective concentration of 12.7 μM SST14 could be deduced from the recorded graph.
evidence: This is based on the FRET competition assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Addition of [Arg8]-vasopressin (AVP) did not restore donor quenching in the FRET competition experiment.
source: In contrast, addition of [Arg8]-vasopressin (AVP), a cyclic neuropeptide of similar size and biochemical characteristics as SST14, did not restore donor quenching in a control experiment, further strengthening the conclusion that the energy transfer reflected a specific interaction between the SST14 donor and Aβ1-42 acceptor.
evidence: This is supported by the FRET competition data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The presence of 15 μM SST14 in the reaction mix reproducibly extended the lag phase of Aβ1-42 aggregation by more than two hours.
source: The application of this method revealed that the presence of 15 μM SST14 (sourced from two independent vendors) in the reaction mix reproducibly extended the lag phase of Aβ1-42 aggregation by more than two hours and lowered the signal amplitude during the subsequent stationary phase (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The presence of 15 μM SST14 lowered the ThT signal amplitude during the stationary phase of Aβ1-42 aggregation.
source: The application of this method revealed that the presence of 15 μM SST14 (sourced from two independent vendors) in the reaction mix reproducibly extended the lag phase of Aβ1-42 aggregation by more than two hours and lowered the signal amplitude during the subsequent stationary phase (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The presence of an intact disulfide bridge within SST14 was not required for the delay in Aβ1-42 aggregation to occur.
source: The presence of an intact disulfide bridge within SST14 was not required for this delay to occur.
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data with reduced SST14 shown in Figure 4B.

claim: No delay in Aβ1-42 aggregation was observed when SST14 was replaced by the AVP negative control peptide.
source: No delay was observed when SST14 was replaced by the AVP negative control peptide.
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pre-incubation of SST14 at a concentration which causes this peptide to pre-aggregate did not affect its ability to delay ThT incorporation into Aβ1-42 aggregates.
source: In further variations to this experimental setup it was established that pre-incubation of SST14, at a concentration which causes this peptide to pre-aggregate (see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1), did not affect its ability to delay ThT incorporation into Aβ1-42 aggregates (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The SST14-dependent lag phase extension correlated directly with the concentration of SST14 in the reaction mix.
source: Importantly, the SST14-dependent lag phase extension correlated directly with the concentration of SST14 in the reaction mix (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by the concentration-dependent Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The presence of SST had no influence on the ThT fluorescence curve collected with a reaction mix containing 10 μM amylin.
source: More specifically, the presence of SST had no influence on the ThT fluorescence curve collected with a reaction mix containing 10 μM amylin. This result was observed even when SST was added to the reaction well at a considerably higher concentration of 100 μM (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data with amylin shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: CST17 is more potent than SST14 in its ability to interfere with Aβ1-42 aggregation-dependent ThT incorporation.
source: Finally, an experiment in which SST14 was replaced by CST17 revealed that the latter peptide is even more potent in its ability to interfere with the Aβ1-42 aggregation-dependent ThT incorporation. Thus, whereas the addition of 15 μM SST14 delayed Aβ1-42 aggregation by a few hours, addition of CST at the same concentration completely abrogated ThT incorporation (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Addition of 15 μM CST17 completely abrogated ThT incorporation in Aβ1-42 aggregation assays.
source: Thus, whereas the addition of 15 μM SST14 delayed Aβ1-42 aggregation by a few hours, addition of CST at the same concentration completely abrogated ThT incorporation (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: SST14 required concentrations upward of 200 μM before it reliably assembled into aggregates that incorporated ThT.
source: At concentrations above 3% w/w (~20 mM) the SST14 peptide had been observed to acquire amyloid characteristics, including Congo Red birefringence (van Grondelle et al., 2007). In our hands, even considerably lower concentrations of SST14 exceeding 250 μM reproducibly caused SST14 to incorporate ThT following a 2 hr lag phase (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of 1 μM pre-aggregated Aβ1-42 caused a profound delay in SST14 aggregation-dependent ThT incorporation.
source: Strikingly, this analysis revealed that the presence of 1 μM Aβ1-42 caused a profound delay in SST14 aggregation-dependent ThT incorporation but only when Aβ1-42 had been allowed to pre-aggregate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The interaction of SST14 with Aβ1-42 relies on the presence of pre-aggregated oAβ1-42.
source: Taken together, these experiments corroborated the notion that the interaction of SST14 with Aβ1-42 relies on the presence of pre-aggregated oAβ1-42.
evidence: This is based on the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data showing that only pre-aggregated Aβ1-42 affects SST14 aggregation.

claim: The incubation of monomeric Aβ1-42 alone over a span of 18 hr caused its signals to gradually shift to higher molecular mass bands.
source: As expected, the incubation of monomeric Aβ1-42 alone over a span of 18 hr caused its signals to gradually shift to higher molecular mass bands, reflecting the appearance of Aβ1-42 aggregates.
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot time-course data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In the presence of SST14 or CST17, 6E10-reactive signals that migrated at the level of monomeric Aβ1-42 disappeared over the course of 18 hr at a slower rate than observed with Aβ1-42 alone.
source: In the presence of SST14 or CST17, 6E10-reactive signals that migrated at the level of monomeric Aβ1-42 also disappeared over the course of 18 hr albeit at a slower rate than observed with Aβ1-42 alone, most likely reflecting the delayed aggregation (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot time-course data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In the presence of SST14 or CST17, only very weak HMM signals of lower apparent molecular weight (50-70 kDa) could be seen following 18 hr incubation.
source: Strikingly, however, in the presence of SST14 or CST17 only very weak HMM signals of lower apparent molecular weight (50-70 kDa) than those seen in preparations of Aβ1-42 alone (55-200 kDa) could be seen following 18 hr incubation (Figure 5B, lanes 8 and 10).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There is an inverse correlation between the signal intensity of SST14 and CST17 concentrations and 6E10-reactive blot signals.
source: To further explore the apparent disappearance of 6E10-reactive bands during this time-course experiment, we next repeated the 18 hr incubation of Aβ1-42 in the presence of varying concentrations of SST14 or CST17. This experiment documented again an inverse correlation of the signal intensity of SST14 and CST17 concentrations and 6E10-reactive blot signals (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The disappearance of 6E10-reactive signals in the presence of SST14 or CST17 was similarly observed with antibodies targeting a central Aβ1-42 epitope (4G8) or the very C-terminus of Aβ1-42 (12F4).
source: This effect was not limited to detection by the 6E10 antibody but was similarly observed with antibodies targeting a central Aβ1-42 epitope (4G8) or the very C-terminus of Aβ1-42 (12F4) (not shown).
evidence: This is based on Western blot experiments with different antibodies.

claim: The interaction of SST14 or CST17 masked the ability of antibodies to bind to Aβ1-42.
source: The disappearance of signals could not be attributed to some unexpected disappearance of the Aβ1-42 peptide in these samples, because silver-stain analyses of the same fractions revealed relatively stronger Aβ1-42 signals in CST17 and SST14 containing samples. Rather, all available data suggest that the interaction of SST14 or CST17 masked the ability of these antibodies to bind to Aβ1-42.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of Western blot and silver-stain data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At higher peptide concentrations, Aβ1-42 and Aβ1-40 exhibited shorter lag phases in the ThT fluorescence assay of 30 min and 45 min, respectively.
source: As expected, at these higher concentrations, Aβ1-42 and Aβ1-40 exhibited shorter lag phases in the ThT fluorescence assay of 30 min and 45 min, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The presence of CST17 (or SST14), but not AVP, extended the lag phase of Aβ aggregation considerably (by approximately one hour).
source: Consistent with the ThT fluorescence data collected at lower peptide concentrations (Figure 4), the presence of CST17 (or SST14, not shown), but not AVP, extended the lag phase of Aβ aggregation considerably (by approximately one hour).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Aβ1-42-containing samples incubated for 18 hr in the presence of SST14 or CST17 gave rise to 6E10-reactive bands that migrated at 50-60 kDa.
source: Interestingly, Aβ1-42-containing samples subjected to the milder treatment, which had been incubated for 18 hr in the presence of SST14 or CST17, gave rise to 6E10-reactive bands that migrated at 50-60 kDa, not seen in samples incubated either without these peptides or with AVP (Figure 6B, lanes 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The 50-60 kDa 6E10-reactive bands were even more pronounced when samples had been boiled in the presence of SDS.
source: These intermediate-sized 6E10-reactive bands were even more pronounced when the same samples had been boiled in the presence of SDS (Figure 6B, lanes 10 and 11) but escaped detection with an antibody directed against the C-terminus of Aβ1-42 (Figure 6B, lanes 6 and 7).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The 50-60 kDa bands escaped detection with an antibody directed against the C-terminus of Aβ1-42.
source: These intermediate-sized 6E10-reactive bands were even more pronounced when the same samples had been boiled in the presence of SDS (Figure 6B, lanes 10 and 11) but escaped detection with an antibody directed against the C-terminus of Aβ1-42 (Figure 6B, lanes 6 and 7).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Similar 50-60 kDa bands were not observed when Aβ1-40 served as the substrate for aggregation.
source: Interestingly, similar bands were not observed when Aβ1-40 served as the substrate for aggregation (Figure 6B, lanes 22 and 23), suggesting that the two most C-terminal residues of Aβ1-42 confer properties that are essential for the formation of the 50-60 kDa oligomeric assemblies.
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The two most C-terminal residues of Aβ1-42 confer properties that are essential for the formation of the 50-60 kDa oligomeric assemblies.
source: Interestingly, similar bands were not observed when Aβ1-40 served as the substrate for aggregation (Figure 6B, lanes 22 and 23), suggesting that the two most C-terminal residues of Aβ1-42 confer properties that are essential for the formation of the 50-60 kDa oligomeric assemblies.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of Aβ1-42 and Aβ1-40 Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Low mass bands that migrated at levels expected for heterodimers of Aβ1-42 and SST14 (or CST17) were occasionally observed in samples that contained SST14 (or CST17).
source: Strikingly, in samples that contained SST14 (or CST17) a fraction of these low mass bands, less than what would be needed for their detection by silver-staining, were occasionally (in well-resolved gels) observed to migrate at levels expected for heterodimers of Aβ1-42 and SST14 (or CST17) (Figure 6B, lanes 5, 6, 10 and 11).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Heterodimers containing SST14 migrated slightly faster than those containing CST17.
source: Consistent with the 3-amino acid smaller size of SST14, relative to CST17, the respective heterodimers containing SST14 migrated slightly faster than those containing CST17.
evidence: This is based on the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A five-fold increase in Aβ1-42 levels in the reaction mix further emphasized the appearance of low mass heterodimers and revealed strong signals migrating at the expected size of Aβ1-42 dimers.
source: A five-fold increase in Aβ1-42 levels in the reaction mix further emphasized the appearance of these low mass heterodimers but also revealed strong signals migrating at the expected size of Aβ1-42 dimers (Figure 6B, lanes 13 to 16).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Evidence for heterotrimers composed of two Aβ1-42 molecules and one SST14 (or CST17) molecule was never obtained.
source: Notably, whereas evidence for heterotrimers composed of two Aβ1-42 molecules and one SST14 (or CST17) molecule was never obtained, we occasionally observed signals that migrated at molecular masses expected for SDS-stable complexes consisting of three Aβ1-42 peptides linked to SST14 (or CST17) (Figure 6B, lanes 14 and 15).
evidence: This is based on the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Signals were occasionally observed that migrated at molecular masses expected for SDS-stable complexes consisting of three Aβ1-42 peptides linked to SST14 (or CST17).
source: Notably, whereas evidence for heterotrimers composed of two Aβ1-42 molecules and one SST14 (or CST17) molecule was never obtained, we occasionally observed signals that migrated at molecular masses expected for SDS-stable complexes consisting of three Aβ1-42 peptides linked to SST14 (or CST17) (Figure 6B, lanes 14 and 15).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Bands matching the size of complexes of three Aβ1-42 peptides linked to SST14 (or CST17) were never observed in fractions lacking SST14 (or CST17) or containing AVP as a negative control peptide.
source: Corroborating this interpretation was the fact that bands matching this size were never observed in fractions lacking SST14 (or CST17) or containing AVP as a negative control peptide.
evidence: This is based on the Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The replacement of tryptophan-8 with alanine, proline, histidine or tyrosine rescued the lag phase extension phenotype in the ThT fluorescence assay.
source: However, when we replaced the single tryptophan present in position 8 both the lag phase extension and the reduction in total ThT fluorescence observed in the presence of wild-type SST were rescued (Figure 7D). This outcome was documented when tryptophan was replaced with alanine, proline, histidine or tyrosine.
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data with SST mutants shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Tryptophan-8 does not merely act by providing an aromatic side-chain but other structural features present in tryptophan provide the necessary fit for binding to Aβ1-42.
source: The fact that even the replacement with tyrosine rescued the lag phase extension phenotype indicates that tryptophan does not merely act in this context by providing an aromatic side-chain but suggests that other structural features present in tryptophan provide the necessary fit for binding to Aβ1-42 in this PBS-based system.
evidence: This is based on the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data with SST mutants shown in Figure 7D.

claim: A peptide encompassing SST residues 5-11 can replace wild-type SST with regard to its effect on Aβ1-42.
source: Analogous experiments with truncated SST peptides revealed that a peptide encompassing SST residues 5-11 can replace wild-type SST with regard to its effect on Aβ1-42 (Figure 7E), thereby upholding the conclusion that the ability of SST to form its internal disulfide bridge is not essential for this effect (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data with truncated SST peptides shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The SST6-10 peptide lacked the ability to influence Aβ1-42 aggregation.
source: However, further stripping of one amino acid from each end of this peptide resulted in a SST6-10 peptide, which lacked the ability to influence Aβ1-42 aggregation.
evidence: This is supported by the Thioflavin T fluorescence assay data with truncated SST peptides shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Aβ aggregates present in ThT aggregation assay fractions after 75 min of incubation were profoundly shifted toward smaller particle sizes when samples were co-incubated with SST.
source: We next compared Aβ aggregate size populations in the presence or absence of SST by nanoparticle tracking analysis (based on Nanosight technology [Filipe et al., 2010]). This orthogonal method documented that Aβ aggregates present in ThT aggregation assay fractions after 75 min of incubation were profoundly shifted toward smaller particle sizes when samples were co-incubated with SST (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the nanoparticle tracking analysis data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The replacement of SST with an SST-W8P negative control peptide did not result in a particle size shift toward smaller aggregates.
source: Importantly, the replacement of SST with an SST-W8P negative control peptide did not result in this particle size shift toward smaller aggregates (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), indicating that the altered particle size distribution is caused by the SST-Aβ interaction, rather than by some unspecific effect of the peptide.
evidence: This is supported by the nanoparticle tracking analysis data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Incubating 50 μM of Aβ1-42 under aggregation conditions resulted in the appearance of characteristic amyloid fibrils.
source: Negative stain electron microscopy corroborated the reduction in aggregate size when Aβ1-42 was incubated with SST versus Aβ1-42 alone (Figure 7—figure supplement 2). Incubating 50 μM of Aβ1-42 under aggregation conditions resulted in the appearance of characteristic amyloid fibrils (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), while in the presence of equimolar concentrations of SST only oligomeric structures were observed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the electron microscopy data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the presence of equimolar concentrations of SST, only oligomeric structures were observed instead of amyloid fibrils.
source: Incubating 50 μM of Aβ1-42 under aggregation conditions resulted in the appearance of characteristic amyloid fibrils (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A), while in the presence of equimolar concentrations of SST only oligomeric structures were observed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the electron microscopy data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Signaling downstream of SST positively modulates transcription of the neprilysin gene.
source: A 2009 milestone report revealed that signaling downstream of SST positively modulates transcription of the neprilysin gene (Saito et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Saito et al., 2005.

claim: An inverse relationship exists between SST and Aβ1-42 levels in mice deficient for the somatostatin gene.
source: Consistent with the known role of neprilysin as one of only a few proteases known to contribute to Aβ1-42 degradation, the authors reported an inverse relationship between SST and Aβ1-42 levels in mice deficient for the somatostatin gene.
evidence: This is based on the findings reported in the cited study (Saito et al., 2005).

claim: Robust tau hyperphosphorylation was observed when mouse hippocampal neurons cultured for 18 days were exposed to oAβ1-42.
source: In agreement with prior data by others, robust tau hyperphosphorylation was observed when mouse hippocampal neurons, which had been cultured for 18 days, were exposed to oAβ1-42 but not when mAβ was added to the cell culture dish (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Tau hyperphosphorylation was not observed when mAβ was added to the cell culture dish.
source: In agreement with prior data by others, robust tau hyperphosphorylation was observed when mouse hippocampal neurons, which had been cultured for 18 days, were exposed to oAβ1-42 but not when mAβ was added to the cell culture dish (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8B.

claim: When primary hippocampal neurons were exposed to SST14 alone, levels of tau phospho-occupancy at pSer202/pThr205 (AT8) were slightly reduced relative to vehicle-treated control cells.
source: When primary hippocampal neurons were exposed to SST14 alone, levels of tau phospho-occupancy at pSer202/pThr205 (AT8) were slightly reduced relative to vehicle-treated control cells.
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8C.

claim: A similar reduction in phospho-occupancy at AT8 was seen when SST14 was replaced with SST28, CST17 or CST29.
source: A similar reduction in phospho-occupancy was seen when SST14 was replaced with SST28 (Figure 8C, lanes 2-5), the longer physiologically relevant and bioactive version of this peptide, or the dominant preprocortistatin-derived regulatory peptides, CST17 or CST29.
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The addition of SST14, SST28, CST17 or CST29 together with oAβ1-42 did not prevent the anticipated tau hyperphosphorylation-inducing effect of oAβ1-42 exposure.
source: The addition of these peptides together with oAβ1-42 did not prevent the anticipated tau hyperphosphosphorylation-inducing effect of oAβ1-42 exposure (Figure 8C, lanes 8-11).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Both SST14 and CST17, but not control peptides, were observed to potentiate tau hyperphosphorylation when Aβ1-42 was concomitantly added in monomeric form to the cell culture medium.
source: Most remarkably, however, both SST14 and CST17, but not the aforementioned control peptides, were observed to potentiate tau hyperphosphorylation under the latter conditions when Aβ1-42 was concomitantly added in monomeric form to the cell culture medium (Figure 8D, lanes 7 and 8).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8D.

claim: SST-dependent tau hyperphosphorylation following co-administration of monomeric Aβ1-42 was not observed every time.
source: This line of investigation was pursued because, in contrast to the oAβ1-42-induced tau hyperphosphorylation phenotype, which was robustly observed, SST-dependent tau hyperphosphorylation following co-administration of monomeric Aβ1-42 was not observed every time.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations from the primary hippocampal neuron assays.

claim: The tau hyperphosphorylation phenotype was reliably observed in three independent biological replicates only when 48 hr pre-aggregated SST14 was added to the cell culture dish.
source: This view is, for instance, corroborated by one series of experiments, in which SST14 pre-aggregation was allowed to proceed for 24 or 48 hr. This experiment led to a tau hyperphosphorylation phenotype in three independent biological replicates only when the 48 hr pre-aggregated SST14 was added to the cell culture dish (Figure 8E, lanes 5, 8 and 11).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The tau hyperphosphorylation phenotype with pre-aggregated SST14 depended on the co-addition of monomeric Aβ1-42.
source: As before, this molecular phenotype depended on the co-addition of monomeric Aβ1-42 and was again not observed when monomeric Aβ1-42 was added to the cell culture medium alone (Figure 8E, lanes 3, 6 and 9).
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assay shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Despite its small size, oAβ1-42 baits were observed to bind reproducibly to more than one hundred proteins in all analyses undertaken.
source: From the large amount of data the study generated, several observations stand out: (1) despite its small size, oAβ1-42 baits were observed to bind reproducibly to more than one hundred proteins in all analyses undertaken
evidence: This is based on the comprehensive interactome data from all three experiments.

claim: When oAβ1-42 was conjugated to the affinity matrix through an N-terminal biotin moiety, a large number of candidate interactors co-enriched with the bait.
source: (2) in particular, when oAβ1-42 was conjugated to the affinity matrix through an N-terminal biotin moiety, a large number of candidate interactors co-enriched with the bait, corroborating a scenario whereby the hydrophobic C-terminal amino acid sequence stretch within Aβ1-42 is probably mostly protein- or lipid-bound
evidence: This is based on the interactome data from Experiment I.

claim: The hydrophobic C-terminal amino acid sequence stretch within Aβ1-42 is probably mostly protein- or lipid-bound.
source: (2) in particular, when oAβ1-42 was conjugated to the affinity matrix through an N-terminal biotin moiety, a large number of candidate interactors co-enriched with the bait, corroborating a scenario whereby the hydrophobic C-terminal amino acid sequence stretch within Aβ1-42 is probably mostly protein- or lipid-bound
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that more proteins bind when the N-terminus is used for tethering, leaving the C-terminus free.

claim: Distinct assemblies of 50-60 kDa, reminiscent of the previously reported Aβ*56, were robustly generated in the presence of SST in reaction mixtures with Aβ1-42 but not with Aβ1-40.
source: (5) distinct assemblies of 50-60 kDa, reminiscent of the previously reported Aβ*56, were robustly generated in the presence of SST in reaction mixtures with Aβ1-42 but not with Aβ1-40
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot and other biochemical data comparing Aβ1-42 and Aβ1-40.

claim: The concomitant exposure of cells to monomeric Aβ and pre-aggregated SST can induce tau hyperphosphorylation at key AD-associated phosphorylation sites.
source: (6) whereas Aβ alone does not induce tau hyperphosphorylation in a primary hippocampal neuron assay, unless it is added to the cell culture medium in a pre-aggregated form, the concomitant exposure of cells to monomeric Aβ and pre-aggregated SST can induce tau hyperphosphorylation at key AD-associated phosphorylation sites.
evidence: This is supported by the Western blot data from the primary hippocampal neuron assays.

claim: Clusterin was previously proposed to represent an Aβ interactor.
source: Several of the oAβ1-42 binders observed in this work, including clusterin (Narayan et al., 2011; Ghiso et al., 1993), 17-β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase X (HSD10) (Yan et al., 1997), the ATP synthase complex (Schmidt et al., 2008), GAPDH (Verdier et al., 2005), and the prion protein (Laurén et al., 2009), had previously been proposed to represent Aβ interactors.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Narayan et al., 2011; Ghiso et al., 1993.

claim: HSD10 initially emerged from a yeast two-hybrid screen as an Aβ binding protein.
